title: Add cost-aware degradation policies and telemetry tags to PRD for granular fallback control
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: A recent regional incident (postmortem: DOC-2026-045-kv-regen) showed that automatic fallbacks and cache rehydration created large unexpected token cost spikes and poor operator visibility. Current PRD language mandates "graceful degradation" but lacks measurable budget semantics, request-level telemetry, and operator controls to prioritize customers during recovery. This ticket translates the postmortem actions into discrete PRD requirements: (1) define cost-aware degradation budgets tied to customer-impact tiers, (2) mandate request-level telemetry tags to explain fallback decisions, and (3) add operator-facing controls and verification harnesses to validate non-regression and SLA alignment.
acceptance_criteria: PRD section added: 'Degradation budgets' with clear budget units (tokens/hour) per customer-impact-tier and mapping table from tier to default budgets
Telemetry tags defined and instrumented (fallback_reason, fallback_budget_label, routed_variant, budget_consumed_ms) and documented in telemetry schema
Operator controls: console UI + API to adjust per-tenant budget labels and force-rollforward with audit logs
Synthetic canary suite (per-degradation-path) that validates: a) fallback triggers within configured budget, b) routing falls back to expected variant, c) cost metric spikes capped to budget envelope
Dashboards and alerting: budget burn rate, atypical fallback density, and rollback triggers wired into existing SLO alerting
Runbook updated: step-by-step actions when budget exhaustion occurs, including customer notification templates and escalation matrix
Non-regression tests: CI integration test that simulates KV cache regen and verifies telemetry tags and budget caps are emitted
Stakeholder signoff: PM, Runtime Eng, Observability, and Support have approved PRD wording and verification matrix
notes: Trade-offs considered: conservative default budgets vs. operational complexity; decided to ship defaults per tier and expose operator config rather than per-customer bespoke rules at launch. Quantization/latency trade-offs noted — some model variants may increase tokens for equivalent quality; PRD will call out a 'quality delta' metric to track customer regressions. This PRD addition is intentionally implementation-agnostic; ENG will own kernel/runtime changes and specific budget enforcement mechanisms.
